questions.stem: At a mobile FinTech startup, the cloud development team is building a serverless document-upload feature where authenticated mobile app users upload 250 MB PDF statements directly to a private Amazon S3 bucket (bypassing API Gateway's 10 MB payload limit). Select and order the 4 architectural steps from login to direct S3 upload.
options: Order 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4: (1) Authenticate the mobile user against an Amazon Cognito User Pool and receive a signed JWT ID/Access token -> (2) Call an Amazon API Gateway REST endpoint (protected by a Cognito User Pool Authorizer) that invokes an AWS Lambda function -> (3) Have the Lambda function (whose Execution Role holds `s3:PutObject` permission) call the S3 SDK `generate_presigned_url('put_object')` with a 15-minute expiration and return the URL to the client -> (4) Have the mobile client perform an HTTP `PUT` of the 250 MB file directly to Amazon S3 using the Pre-Signed URL.
Order 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1: (1) Upload the 250 MB PDF directly through API Gateway -> (2) Invoke Lambda -> (3) Generate a Pre-Signed URL after upload -> (4) Authenticate with Cognito last.
Order 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 2: (1) Authenticate with Cognito -> (2) Embed static IAM root access keys inside the mobile app binary -> (3) Upload to S3 -> (4) Call API Gateway.
Order 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 4: (1) Call API Gateway unauthenticated -> (2) Make the S3 bucket completely public -> (3) Generate a Pre-Signed URL with no IAM permissions -> (4) Upload via SQS.
questions.explanation: Because Amazon API Gateway enforces a hard 10 MB payload ceiling and 29-second timeout, large binary uploads always authenticate via Cognito (Step 1), request a short-lived S3 Pre-Signed URL from a Lambda function whose Execution Role has `s3:PutObject` permission (Steps 2-3), and upload directly from the client to S3 via HTTP PUT (Step 4). Architectural Deep Dive: AWS Lambda executes serverless functions up to 15 minutes with 128 MB to 10 GB memory, 512 MB to 10 GB /tmp ephemeral storage, Lambda Layers for shared libraries/dependencies across functions, Provisioned Concurrency (or Lambda SnapStart for Java/Python/.NET) to eliminate cold starts, and Reserved Concurrency to guarantee and cap maximum concurrent executions for a specific function. Why Distractors Fail: Option B (Order 4 -> 3 -> 2 -> 1: (1) Upload the 250 MB PDF directly through API Gate...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and confuses Reserved Concurrency (which throttles/caps concurrency and does NOT pre-warm execution environments) with Provisioned Concurrency (which pre-warms environments to eliminate cold-start latency). Option C (Order 1 -> 3 -> 4 -> 2: (1) Authenticate with Cognito -> (2) Embed static I...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and exceeds API Gateway's hard 29-second integration timeout or 10 MB payload ceiling instead of using S3 Pre-Signed URLs for large file uploads or asynchronous invocation patterns. Option D (Order 2 -> 1 -> 3 -> 4: (1) Call API Gateway unauthenticated -> (2) Make th...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and exceeds API Gateway's hard 29-second integration timeout or 10 MB payload ceiling instead of using S3 Pre-Signed URLs for large file uploads or asynchronous invocation patterns.
questions.use_case: Latency-sensitive checkout APIs configure an Application Auto Scaling schedule on Lambda Provisioned Concurrency (pointed at a published function Version or Alias, never $LATEST) ahead of flash sales.
questions.hack: Eliminate Lambda cold starts = Provisioned Concurrency (or SnapStart for Java) on a Version/Alias. Cap a function so it doesn't overwhelm a downstream RDS DB = Reserved Concurrency. Share common SDKs/certs across functions = Lambda Layers.

questions.stem: At a SaaS B2B workflow automation company running event-driven workloads on AWS, a backend developer maintains a mission-critical application that uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest and process large streams of data records in real time. Amazon EC2 instances consume and process the data from the shards of the Kinesis data stream by using Amazon Kinesis Client Library (KCL). The application handles the failure scenarios and does not require standby workers. The application reports that a specific shard is receiving more data than expected. To adapt to the changes in the rate of data flow, the `hot` shard is resharded. Assuming that the initial number of shards in the Kinesis data stream is 4, and after resharding the number of shards increased to 6, what is the maximum number of EC2 instances that can be deployed to process data from all the shards?
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Option B (6.). Amazon Kinesis Data Streams provides sub-second real-time stream ingestion with configurable retention (24 hours up to 365 days), replayability across multiple independent consumers, and optional Enhanced Fan-Out (2 MB/s dedicated throughput per consumer per shard via HTTP/2). Furthermore, Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed, no-code integration service that securely transfers data bidirectionally between SaaS applications (such as Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, Marketo, SAP, and Slack) and AWS services like Amazon S3 and Amazon Redshift - supporting event-driven triggers, scheduled incremental pulls, inline filtering, and AWS PrivateLink. Why Distractors Fail: Option A (12....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option C (4....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option D (1....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt.
questions.use_case: High-velocity clickstream and payment fraud pipelines ingest events into Kinesis Data Streams in On-Demand mode (or Provisioned shards with 1 MB/s write and 2 MB/s read per shard) so Apache Flink, AWS Lambda, and Firehose can all read the exact same stream concurrently.
questions.hack: Multiple consumers needing real-time replay + ordering per PartitionKey = Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Enhanced Fan-Out when multiple consumers need dedicated 2 MB/s read bandwidth without throttling.

questions.stem: [A healthcare patient-portal engineering team deploying containerized and serverless APIs on AWS has a developer who] A startup s photo-sharing site is deployed in a VPC. An ELB distributes web traffic across two subnets. ELB session stickiness is configured to use the AWS-generated session cookie, with a session TTL of 5 minutes. The webserver Auto Scaling Group is configured as: `min-size=4`, `max-size=4`, The startups preparing for a public launch, by running load-testing software installed on a single EC2 instance running in `us-west-2`. After 60 minutes of load-testing, the webserver logs show. Which recommendations can help ensure load-testing HTTP requests are evenly distributed across the four webservers? (Choose TWO)

Re-configure the load-testing software to re-resolve DNS for each web request.
Implement the workflow using a 3rd-party load-testing service which offers globally-distributed test clients.
Configure ELB and Auto Scaling to distribute across `us-west-2a` and `us-west-2c`.
Configure ELB session stickiness to use the app-specific session cookie.

Amazon DynamoDB delivers single-digit millisecond NoSQL performance: 1 RCU supports one strongly consistent read per second (or two eventually consistent reads/sec) for items up to 4 KB, and 1 WCU supports one write/sec up to 1 KB; LSIs share the base table's partition key and must be created at table creation (supporting strong consistency), while GSIs can use any partition/sort key and be added anytime (eventual consistency only). Furthermore, AWS CodeBuild compiles source code, runs unit tests, and produces deployment artifacts according to `buildspec.yml` phases (`install` -> `pre_build` -> `build` -> `post_build`) while natively injecting sensitive parameters from SSM Parameter Store (`env.parameter-store`) or AWS Secrets Manager (`env.secrets-manager`) and caching dependencies in S3 or local Docker layer cache. Why Distractors Fail: Option A (Launch and run the load-tester EC2 instance from `us-east-1` instead....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option D (Configure ELB and Auto Scaling to distribute across `us-west-2a` and `us-we...) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option E (Configure ELB session stickiness to use the app-specific session cookie....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt.
questions.use_case: To prevent concurrent overwrites on an inventory item in DynamoDB, developers enable Optimistic Locking using a version number attribute (@DynamoDBVersionAttribute or ConditionExpression on version); to cache hot reads in microseconds without rewriting SDK queries, they deploy DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
questions.hack: DynamoDB Golden Math: 1 RCU = 4 KB Strong (or 2x4 KB Eventual); 1 WCU = 1 KB. Add new Partition Key query pattern on existing table = GSI (Eventual reads only). Microsecond read cache for hot keys = DAX.

questions.stem: At a real-time logistics tracking provider operating high-throughput REST and GraphQL APIs on AWS, a cloud developer is currently building a stock trading application that requires sub-millisecond latency in processing trading requests. Amazon DynamoDB is used to store all the trading data that is used to process each request. After load testing the application, the development team found that due to data retrieval times, the latency requirement is not satisfied. Because of sudden high spikes in the number of requests, DynamoDB read capacity has to be significantly over-provisioned to avoid throttling. What steps should be taken to meet latency requirements and reduce the cost of running the application?
options: Add Global Secondary Indexes for trading data.
Store trading data in Amazon S3 and use Transfer Acceleration.
Add retries with exponential back-off for DynamoDB queries.
Use DynamoDB Accelerator to cache trading data.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Option D (Use DynamoDB Accelerator to cache trading data.). Amazon Kinesis Data Streams provides sub-second real-time stream ingestion with configurable retention (24 hours up to 365 days), replayability across multiple independent consumers, and optional Enhanced Fan-Out (2 MB/s dedicated throughput per consumer per shard via HTTP/2). Furthermore, Amazon DynamoDB delivers single-digit millisecond NoSQL performance: 1 RCU supports one strongly consistent read per second (or two eventually consistent reads/sec) for items up to 4 KB, and 1 WCU supports one write/sec up to 1 KB; LSIs share the base table's partition key and must be created at table creation (supporting strong consistency), while GSIs can use any partition/sort key and be added anytime (eventual consistency only). Why Distractors Fail: Option A (Add Global Secondary Indexes for trading data....) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and attempts to run strongly consistent reads against a Global Secondary Index (GSI) or tries to add a Local Secondary Index (LSI) to an existing table after creation. Option B (Store trading data in Amazon S3 and use Transfer Acceleration....) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and routes multi-gigabyte file uploads through a Lambda function or EC2 web tier instead of generating an S3 Pre-Signed URL for direct client-to-S3 upload, or forgets that S3 Pre-Signed URLs inherit the exact IAM permissions and session expiration of the principal that generated them. Option C (Add retries with exponential back-off for DynamoDB queries....) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and attempts to run strongly consistent reads against a Global Secondary Index (GSI) or tries to add a Local Secondary Index (LSI) to an existing table after creation.
questions.use_case: High-velocity clickstream and payment fraud pipelines ingest events into Kinesis Data Streams in On-Demand mode (or Provisioned shards with 1 MB/s write and 2 MB/s read per shard) so Apache Flink, AWS Lambda, and Firehose can all read the exact same stream concurrently.
questions.hack: Multiple consumers needing real-time replay + ordering per PartitionKey = Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Enhanced Fan-Out when multiple consumers need dedicated 2 MB/s read bandwidth without throttling.

questions.stem: A digital banking engineering squad enforcing strict zero-trust security and CI/CD governance on AWS has a developer who manages an environment that has 25,000 employees and is growing. The enterprise is creating an application that will be accessible to its employees only. A developer is using Amazon S3 to store images and Amazon RDS to store application data. The enterprise requires that all employee information remain in the legacy Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) employee directory only and is not interested in mirroring any employee information on AWS. How can the cloud engineer provide authorized access for the employees who will be using this application so each employee can access their own application data only?
options: Use Amazon VPC and keep all resources inside the VPC, and use a VPC link for the S3 bucket with the bucket policy.
Use Amazon Cognito user pools, federate with the SAML provider, and use user pool groups with an IAM policy.

Implement the workflow using a Amazon Cognito identity pool, federate with the SAML provider, and use an IAM condition key with a value for the `cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub` variable to grant access to the employees.
Establish and deploy a unique IAM role for each employee and have each employee assume the role to access the application so they can access their personal data only.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Option C (Implement the workflow using a Amazon Cognito identity pool, federate with the SAML provider, and use an IAM condition key with a value for the `cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub` variable to grant access to the employees.). Amazon Cognito separates authentication from AWS resource authorization: Cognito User Pools are managed user directories that handle sign-up, sign-in, MFA, SAML/OIDC social federation, and issue JWT tokens (ID/Access/Refresh) for API Gateway/ALB; Cognito Identity Pools (Federated Identities) exchange a valid login token for temporary, scoped AWS IAM credentials via AWS STS so mobile/web clients can access S3 or DynamoDB directly. Furthermore, AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model) extends CloudFormation (`Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`) to define serverless apps concisely (`AWS::Serverless::Function`, `SimpleTable`, `Api`), supports local testing (`sam local invoke`, `sam local start-api`), uses the `Globals` section to avoid repeating shared properties (Runtime, Timeout, Tracing), and integrates natively with AWS CodeDeploy (`AutoPublishAlias` + `DeploymentPreference` like `Canary10Percent10Minutes` or `Linear10PercentEvery1Minute` with `PreTraffic` and `PostTraffic` Lambda hooks). Why Distractors Fail: Option A (Use Amazon VPC and keep all resources inside the VPC, and use a VPC link fo...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and hardcodes plaintext credentials inside `buildspec.yml` or forgets to configure CodeBuild VPC subnet/NAT settings when build tests must reach private RDS databases. Option B (Use Amazon Cognito user pools, federate with the SAML provider, and use use...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and exceeds API Gateway's hard 29-second integration timeout or 10 MB payload ceiling instead of using S3 Pre-Signed URLs for large file uploads or asynchronous invocation patterns. Option D (Establish and deploy a unique IAM role for each employee and have each empl...) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt.
questions.use_case: A mobile photo app authenticates users via a Cognito User Pool (or Google/Apple login) and then exchanges that token at a Cognito Identity Pool to obtain temporary STS credentials restricted by an IAM policy using ${cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:sub} to the user's own S3 prefix.
questions.hack: Need JWT tokens for API Gateway/ALB login? -> Cognito User Pool. Need temporary AWS IAM credentials for mobile/browser clients to access S3/DynamoDB directly? -> Cognito Identity Pool.

questions.stem: At a media-streaming subscription service scaling globally across multiple AWS Regions, the platform development team is currently using AWS CodePipeline to deliver one of its applications. The delivery pipeline is triggered by changes to the master branch of an AWS CodeCommit repository and uses AWS CodeBuild to implement the test and build stages of the process and AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the application. The pipeline has been operating successfully for several months and there have been no modifications. Following a recent change to the application's source code, AWS CodeDeploy has not deployed the updates application as expected. What are the possible causes? (Choose TWO)
options: The change was not made in the master branch of the AWS CodeCommit repository.
One of the earlier stages in the pipeline failed and the pipeline has terminated.
One of the Amazon EC2 instances in the company's AWS CodePipeline cluster is inactive.
The AWS CodePipeline is incorrectly configured and is not executing AWS CodeDeploy.
AWS CodePipeline does not have permissions to access AWS CodeCommit.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (A, B): Option A (The change was not made in the master branch of the AWS CodeCommit repository.); Option B (One of the earlier stages in the pipeline failed and the pipeline has terminated.). AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model) extends CloudFormation (`Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31`) to define serverless apps concisely (`AWS::Serverless::Function`, `SimpleTable`, `Api`), supports local testing (`sam local invoke`, `sam local start-api`), uses the `Globals` section to avoid repeating shared properties (Runtime, Timeout, Tracing), and integrates natively with AWS CodeDeploy (`AutoPublishAlias` + `DeploymentPreference` like `Canary10Percent10Minutes` or `Linear10PercentEvery1Minute` with `PreTraffic` and `PostTraffic` Lambda hooks). Furthermore, AWS CodeDeploy automates application deployments to EC2/On-Premises, ECS, and Lambda driven by `appspec.yml` in the root directory: for EC2, lifecycle hooks execute in strict order (`ApplicationStop` -> `DownloadBundle` -> `BeforeInstall` -> `Install` -> `AfterInstall` -> `ApplicationStart` -> `ValidateService`); for Lambda and ECS, only `BeforeAllowTraffic` and `AfterAllowTraffic` hooks are used during traffic shifting. Why Distractors Fail: Option C (One of the Amazon EC2 instances in the company's AWS CodePipeline cluster i...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and hardcodes plaintext credentials inside `buildspec.yml` or forgets to configure CodeBuild VPC subnet/NAT settings when build tests must reach private RDS databases. Option D (The AWS CodePipeline is incorrectly configured and is not executing AWS Cod...) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and writes hundreds of lines of raw CloudFormation boilerplate or attempts to run CodeDeploy EC2 shell scripts (`BeforeInstall`/`AfterInstall`) for serverless Lambda traffic shifting. Option E (AWS CodePipeline does not have permissions to access AWS CodeCommit....) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and hardcodes plaintext credentials inside `buildspec.yml` or forgets to configure CodeBuild VPC subnet/NAT settings when build tests must reach private RDS databases.
questions.use_case: Serverless teams define `AutoPublishAlias: live` and `DeploymentPreference: Type: Canary10Percent15Minutes` with CloudWatch `Alarms` in `template.yaml` so CodeDeploy shifts 10% of Lambda traffic, runs a `PreTraffic` validation hook, and automatically rolls back if errors spike.
questions.hack: SAM CLI sequence: `sam build` -> `sam local invoke` (local Docker test) -> `sam package` / `sam deploy --guided`. Safe Lambda traffic shifting = SAM `AutoPublishAlias` + `DeploymentPreference` (CodeDeploy Canary/Linear).

questions.stem: An InsurTech underwriting platform team refactoring legacy monoliths into AWS Lambda and DynamoDB has a developer who maintains a mission-critical application that deployed on AWS Elastic Beanstalk experiences increased error rates during deployments of new application versions, resulting in service degradation for users. The Development team believes that this is because of the reduction in capacity during the deployment steps. The team would like to change the deployment policy configuration of the environment to an option that maintains full capacity during deployment while using the existing instances. Which deployment policy will meet these requirements while using the existing instances?

Rolling.

Immutable.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Option C (Rolling with additional batch.). questions.stem: [a gaming backend studio serving millions of concurrent mobile players on AWS] A company's fleet of Amazon EC2 instances receives data from millions of users through an API. questions.stem: [A travel-booking aggregator integrating third-party partner webhooks through Amazon API Gateway and EventBridge has a developer who] A Developer migrated a web application to AWS. As part of the migration, the cloud engineer implemented an automated continuous integration/continuous improvement (CI/CD) process using a blue/green deployment. The deployment provisions new Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a new Application Load Balancer. After the migration was completed, the cloud engineer began receiving complaints from users getting booted out of the system. The system also requires users to log in after every new deployment. How can these issues be resolved?
options: Use rolling updates instead of a blue/green deployment.
Externalize the user sessions to Amazon ElastiCache.
Turn on sticky sessions in the Application Load Balancer.
Use multicast to replicate session information.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Option B (Externalize the user sessions to Amazon ElastiCache.). Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow) runs open-source Apache Airflow DAGs written in Python for complex cross-platform data orchestration, whereas AWS Step Functions provides serverless visual state-machine orchestration (Standard Workflows for long-running up to 1 year and Express Workflows for high-volume <5 minute event processing). Furthermore, Amazon API Gateway manages REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs with hard limits (29-second integration timeout -> 504 Gateway Timeout; 10 MB payload limit), Stage Variables for pointing dev/stage/prod stages at different Lambda aliases, Canary Release deployments for traffic splitting, Usage Plans + API Keys for per-client throttling/quotas, and Cognito User Pool or Lambda Authorizers for authentication. Why Distractors Fail: Option A (Use rolling updates instead of a blue/green deployment....) is incorrect because that service applies to a different workload pattern and places `appspec.yml` in a nested subdirectory without configuring the path or uses EC2 lifecycle hooks (`BeforeInstall`) inside a Serverless Lambda deployment. Option C (Turn on sticky sessions in the Application Load Balancer....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option D (Use multicast to replicate session information....) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt.
questions.use_case: Teams migrating existing Python Airflow DAGs to AWS choose Amazon MWAA; teams building new AWS-native serverless ETL pipelines with native Glue/Athena/EMR/Lambda SDK integrations and Distributed Map (up to 10,000 parallel executions) choose AWS Step Functions.
questions.hack: Existing Apache Airflow Python DAGs / cross-cloud portability = Amazon MWAA. Serverless AWS-native orchestration / Distributed Map over S3 = AWS Step Functions.

questions.stem: [an IoT smart-home device manufacturer processing real-time telemetry with AWS serverless services] A company maintains a REST service using Amazon API Gateway and the API Gateway native API key validation. The enterprise recently launched a new registration page, which allows users to sign up for the service. The registration page creates a new API key using `CreateApiKey` and sends the new key to the user. When the user attempts to call the API using this key, the user receives a `403 Forbidden` error. Existing users are unaffected and can still call the API. What code updates will grant these new users access to the API?
options: The `createDeployment` method must be called so the API can be redeployed to include the newly created API key.
The `updateAuthorizer` method must be called to update the API's authorizer to include the newly created API key.
The `importApiKeys` method must be called to import all newly created API keys into the current stage of the API.
The `createUsagePlanKey` method must be called to associate the newly created API key with the correct usage plan.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Option D (The `createUsagePlanKey` method must be called to associate the newly created API key with the correct usage plan.). Amazon API Gateway manages REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs with hard limits (29-second integration timeout -> 504 Gateway Timeout; 10 MB payload limit), Stage Variables for pointing dev/stage/prod stages at different Lambda aliases, Canary Release deployments for traffic splitting, Usage Plans + API Keys for per-client throttling/quotas, and Cognito User Pool or Lambda Authorizers for authentication. Why Distractors Fail: Option A (The `createDeployment` method must be called so the API can be redeployed t...) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option B (The `updateAuthorizer` method must be called to update the API's authorizer...) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt. Option C (The `importApiKeys` method must be called to import all newly created API k...) fails to satisfy the specific performance, security, or managed-service constraint stated in the prompt.
questions.use_case: When browser Single-Page Applications (SPAs) receive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) errors calling a cross-domain REST API, developers enable CORS on the API Gateway resource so OPTIONS preflight requests return Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, and Access-Control-Allow-Headers.
questions.hack: API Gateway Shortcuts: 504 error = Backend exceeded 29s timeout; 429 error = Throttling limit exceeded; Upload >10 MB file = Return an S3 Pre-Signed URL; Authenticate with 3rd-party OAuth/JWT bearer token = Lambda Authorizer.

questions.stem: A cloud-native EdTech platform automating multi-environment deployments with AWS SAM and CDK has a developer who is currently building an application to track athlete performance using an Amazon DynamoDB table. Each item in the table is identified by a partition key (`user_id`) and a sort key (`sport_name`). The table design is shown below. (Note: Not all table attributes are shown) A Developer is asked to write a leaderboard application to display the top performers (`user_id`) based on the score for each `sport_name`. questions.stem: At a regulated financial clearinghouse auditing API latency and distributed traces with AWS X-Ray, a developer is currently migrating a single-server, on-premises web application to AWS. options: An Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster.

The web server's primary disk.
An Amazon EC2 instance dedicated to session data.
questions.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Option A (An Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster.). questions.stem: [An enterprise HR-tech platform migrating deployment pipelines to AWS CodePipeline and CodeDeploy has a developer who] A Development team is working on a case management solution that allows medical claims to be processed and reviewed.
